title: Bricks Hurled at Ohio Hindu Temple During Prayers, Windows Shattered
excerpt: The Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights was struck around 1:30 pm on Friday while priests and devotees were inside. No arrests have been reported, and surveillance footage is under review.
body:
• Bricks were hurled at the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights, Ohio, around 1:30 pm on Friday, October 2, shattering windows while priests and devotees were inside.
  • The Hindu American Foundation (HAF) said surveillance footage is being reviewed by authorities and that it has alerted the FBI and its Civil Rights division; no suspect has been publicly identified and no arrests reported.
  • The Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) called on Richmond Heights Mayor Kim Thomas to condemn the attack and urged swift police action, describing it as possible hate-motivated violence.
  • For Hindu-American readers: report threats or attacks on places of worship to local police and the FBI's Civil Rights division; HAF says it is in contact with temple leaders and offering assistance, and both groups urge community members to document and report incidents promptly.

Temple struck during Friday prayers

A Hindu temple in Ohio's Greater Cleveland area was attacked with bricks on Friday afternoon while worshippers were inside, causing significant damage to the building. The incident took place at the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights, at around 1:30 pm local time, according to the Hindu American Foundation (HAF), the US-based nonprofit that first reported the attack.

Bricks thrown at the temple shattered windows and caused significant damage to the structure, HAF said in a post on X. Priests and devotees were present inside the temple at the time of the attack. The organisation said surveillance footage of the incident is available and is being reviewed by authorities. No injuries have been reported, and neither HAF nor the Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) has disclosed how many windows were damaged.

"This possible hate crime comes at a time of unprecedented hate & vitriol directed at the Hindu American community, and we ask that law enforcement make apprehending the perpetrator(s) a top priority."

— Hindu American Foundation

HAF said it has alerted the FBI and its Civil Rights division and is in touch with temple leaders, offering all assistance. The foundation urged the nation's elected leaders and government agencies to "publicly & unequivocally condemn hateful rhetoric against Indian and Hindu American communities." CoHNA separately pressed Richmond Heights Mayor Kim Thomas and city authorities to condemn the attack: "We call upon Mayor Kim Thomas and @RichmondHtsOH to condemn such bigotry and @PoliceRichmond to take swift action against the perpetrator," the coalition said. No suspect has been publicly identified, and authorities have not confirmed a religious motive, ANI reported.

Attack lands at a charged moment for the community

The attack came as Hindu communities in Ohio began observing Hindu Heritage Month, which Hindu organisations across the US mark each October, and days before Navratri celebrations. The HAF post noted that the incident also coincided with the anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi's birth, a day of significance for Indian and Hindu-American communities.

The episode fits a documented pattern of vandalism against Hindu places of worship in the United States that CoHNA has been tracking. Its published chronology includes the vandalism of a Mahatma Gandhi statue at Shri Tulsi Mandir in Queens, New York, in August 2022; hateful graffiti at the SMVS Shri Swaminarayan Temple in Newark, California, in December 2023; vandalism at BAPS temples in Melville, New York, and the Sacramento area of California in September 2024; and the defacing of a BAPS temple in Chino Hills, California, with messages targeting the Hindu community in March 2025.

Hindu-American advocacy groups say these incidents are drawing attention to the security of religious institutions at a moment when the community reports rising hostility. CoHNA has documented the pattern as part of a broader campaign to press law enforcement agencies to treat temple attacks as potential hate crimes and to prioritise apprehension of perpetrators.

What it means for Hindu Americans

The attack struck a working temple during active worship, which raises the stakes for community safety planning well beyond the damage to the building itself. Temples in the US function as both religious and community centres for local Hindu families — many of them Indian-American — and incidents like this tend to reverberate quickly through diaspora networks.

For Hindu Americans, the immediate practical consequence is heightened attention to temple security ahead of Navratri, one of the busiest festival periods of the year, when temples expect larger crowds. Both HAF and CoHNA have urged community members to document and report incidents promptly: attacks on places of worship can be reported to local police and to the FBI's Civil Rights division. HAF said it is coordinating directly with the Richmond Heights temple's leadership and offering assistance, a channel other temples facing threats can approach through the foundation.

The call for elected officials to condemn the attack also reflects a broader push by Hindu-American groups for political recognition of anti-Hindu hate as a distinct concern in American civil-rights discourse. Whether Richmond Heights officials and federal authorities respond publicly will be watched as a signal of how seriously such incidents are being taken at the local and federal level.

What to watch next

The investigation is in its early stages: surveillance footage is under review, no suspect has been named, and no motive has been established. The next developments to watch are whether Richmond Heights police or the FBI make an arrest, whether Mayor Kim Thomas and city officials issue a public condemnation as CoHNA has demanded, and whether any federal assessment of a hate-crime charge follows. With Navratri beginning shortly, community organisations will also be watching whether local authorities step up security coordination with temples in the Greater Cleveland area.
image_caption: Shattered glass lies scattered across the floor inside the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir after the attack. The Richmond Heights, Ohio temple was struck with bricks on Friday afternoon while priests and devotees were inside.
nri_angle: The attack targeted a place of worship for Hindu Americans in Ohio during prayers, sharpening community fears about temple safety and the response to anti-Hindu hate in the US.
